guide.title: Ask the guide
guide.intro: Ask how to use ilovelawyer. The guide answers here and lights up the right button. Legal questions go to Consultation, where answers cite their sources.
guide.legalAnswer: That's a legal question, so it belongs in a Consultation, where answers come with citations.
guide.fallbackAnswer: I can help with using ilovelawyer: opening cases, uploading documents, the Legal Terminal, the calendar or your team. Try “How do I open a case in the Legal Terminal?”
guide.tourWorkspace: Tour the Workspace on a sample case
guide.tourTerminal: Tour the Terminal on a sample case
guide.trySample: Try it on a sample case

answers.terminal: Every case row has two ways in. Choose **Legal Terminal** for the full pane grid, or **Workspace** for chat and sources.
answers.terminal_blocked: The **Legal Terminal** opens from a case, and you don't have one yet. **Create a case** first, and I'll take you the rest of the way.
answers.terminal_next: Your case is ready. Choose **Legal Terminal** on its row to open the full pane grid.
answers.upload: Use the **attach** button in the composer to add a contract or filing. Inside a case, the Documents section has its own **Upload** button.
answers.newCase: New matters start from **New case** on the Cases page. The wizard asks for the caption, the parties and any documents.
answers.calendar: Hearings and deadlines live in the **Calendar**. Link an event to a case and it shows up as the Terminal's next date.
answers.team: Invites and member roles are under **Organization** in the account menu.
answers.team_UK: Invites and member roles are under **Organisation** in the account menu.
answers.theme: The **sun / moon** button in the header switches between light and dark.
answers.library: Codals, jurisprudence and Republic Acts are in the **Library**.
answers.library_UK: UK case law and legislation are in the **Library**.
answers.voice: Tap the **microphone** in the composer to dictate. Your words appear in the box so you can edit them before sending.
answers.newConsultation: Use the **+** button at the top of the consultation sidebar to start a new consultation. Earlier ones stay in the history.
answers.history: Your past consultations are in the **history** sidebar on the left of Consultation.
answers.findCase: Search by case name or party in the **search box** at the top of the Cases page.
answers.statusFilter: Use the **Active / Archived** toggle to switch between your current and archived cases. Archived cases keep all their documents.
answers.workspace: Every case has a **Workspace**. It opens sources, chat and Studio side by side, where you can make an audio overview, mind map or case brief.
answers.workspace_blocked: Audio overviews, mind maps and case briefs are made inside a case, and you don't have one yet. **Create a case** first, and I'll take you the rest of the way.
answers.workspace_next: Your case is ready. Open its **Workspace** and add documents under Sources. Studio makes audio overviews, mind maps and case briefs from them.
answers.notifications: The **bell** in the header shows indexing, hearing and comment alerts. Unread ones have a gold count.
answers.language: Switch between English, Tagalog and Korean from the **language** menu in the header.
answers.profile: Your name, username and password are under **Profile** in the account menu.
answers.tour: You can replay the tour from **Ask the guide**: open it and choose Replay the tour.
answers.librarySearch: Type a topic, a code or a G.R. number into the **Library search** to find matching authorities.
answers.librarySearch_UK: Type a case name, a neutral citation or an Act title into the **Library search** to find matching authorities.
answers.libraryCategories: Use the **category tabs** beside the search box to switch between decisions and statutes.
answers.libraryCategories_UK: Use the **category tabs** beside the search box to switch between case law and legislation.
answers.libraryFilters: The **filters** under the search box narrow results by case type, topic or court.
answers.libraryFilters_UK: The **court filter** under the search box narrows case law by court.
answers.addEvent: Pick a day, then press **+** in the day panel. Choose Appointment or Note, set the time and link a case.
answers.reminder: When you **add** an event, set a reminder and an optional email to notify.
answers.editEvent: Select the day, then edit or delete the event from the **day panel**.
answers.month: The **month grid** shows every hearing, deadline and note at a glance. Pick a day to see its events.

sources.title: Your documents
sources.body: Every file in the case, by folder. Tick a document to include it in chat answers. Each one shows whether it's indexed and ready.

chat.title: Ask about this case
chat.body: Chat answers only from the ticked documents, and every claim cites the file and page it came from.

tiles.title: Studio makes things from the case
tiles.body: Each tile builds something from the same documents. You'll open each one next.

audio.title: Audio Overview
audio.body: Two hosts talk through the facts and the issues. Generate the script, then render audio you can play or download.

mindmap.title: Mind Map
mindmap.body: The case as a strategy map: facts, law, the other side's theory, gaps and next steps. Expand any node for more.

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.body: Dates found in your documents, in order. Each event says which document it came from.

datatable.title: Data Table
datatable.body: Witnesses, damages, deadlines and findings from the whole case, in one table.

decisions.title: Decisions
decisions.body: The reasoning behind each legal answer. If a fact changes, dispute it and the answer is flagged.

brief.title: Case brief
brief.body: Facts, issues, arguments and relief sought, ready to download as PDF or Word.

terminal.name: Terminal
terminal.done: Terminal tour complete. Add more panes any time from Add pane.

nextdate.title: The next date, always in view
nextdate.body: This chip shows the case's next hearing or deadline, taken from the Calendar.

command.title: Case Summary: start here
command.body: Case health, the next date and your next actions, all on one card.

evidence.title: Evidence & Timeline
evidence.body: Everything you upload lands here, linked to its source, with its status: verified, needs authenticating, or disputed.

law.title: Law & Precedent
law.body: Statutes and decisions for this case. Check a quote against the source, or look for rulings that go against you.

legalIssues.title: Legal Issues
legalIssues.body: What the court must decide, and who carries the burden on each. Mark them off as you brief them.

procedure.title: Case Strategy
procedure.body: Your filing checklist and deadlines. They move on their own when a key date moves.

redTeam.title: Red Team
redTeam.body: The strongest case against your position, so nothing in court surprises you.

whatChanged.title: What changed
whatChanged.body: Each time the analysis runs, after a refresh or a new document, a gold dot appears here. Press it to see what moved.

changeHistory.title: Every run, pane by pane
changeHistory.body: What each run changed in every pane, next to the edits your team made by hand. Open jumps straight to the pane.

addPane.title: 21 panes, five groups
addPane.body: Add pane opens every panel, grouped by Facts, Law, Strategy, Risk and Team, each with a one-line description.

arrange.title: Make it yours
arrange.body: Switch between Free, Columns and Focus. Pin a pane to lock it in place, and save layouts for different kinds of work.

pageTour.nothing: There's nothing on this page to point at right now.

steps.consult-history: Your past consultations. Open one to pick up where you left off.
steps.cases-new: Start a new case: name the matter, add the parties and attach documents.
steps.cases-search: Find a case by its name or a party.
steps.cases-filters: Switch between your active and archived cases. Archived cases keep all their documents.
steps.case-row-workspace: Open a case's Workspace: its documents, chat and Studio side by side.
steps.case-row-terminal: Open a case in the Legal Terminal: the full grid of analysis panes.
steps.library-search: Search codals, jurisprudence and Republic Acts by topic, title or G.R. number.
steps.library-search_UK: Search UK case law and legislation by case name, neutral citation or Act title.
steps.library-cats_UK: Switch between case law and legislation.
steps.library-filters: Narrow the results by case type, topic or court.
steps.cal-grid: Your month at a glance. Days with hearings, deadlines or notes are marked; pick one to see it.
steps.cal-day: The selected day's appointments and notes. Edit or delete them here.
steps.cal-add: Add an appointment or a note to the selected day, link a case and set a reminder.
steps.cases-create-first: Workspace and the Legal Terminal open from a case. Create one, and both appear on its row.

studio.title: Studio
studio.body: Make an audio overview, mind map, timeline or case brief from a case's documents.

consultation.title: Consultation
consultation.body: Ask in plain language. Answers cite the codals and decisions they rely on.
consultation.body_UK: Ask in plain language. Answers cite the legislation and judgments they rely on.

sample.question: Is this estafa or an unpaid debt?
sample.question_UK: Is this fraud or an unpaid debt?
sample.answer: Estafa needs deceit before or at the time the money was handed over. A promise broken later is a civil debt.
sample.answer_UK: Fraud by false representation needs a dishonest statement made to gain. A promise broken later is usually a civil debt.
